B. Is this measure already running in North Savo wellbeing services county (or in the KYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Fitness assessment and prehabilitation before deciding against curative treatment. Before a stage I-III patient is judged too frail, they get an exercise test, a geriatric assessment if over 75, and four weeks of supervised exercise, breathing training and help to stop smoking. Then the decision is made again.
supported_en: A Cochrane review from 2022 (9 trials, 573 patients) found that exercise before lung cancer surgery cuts lung complications after surgery by more than half (RR 0.45).
not_supported_en: No page we read measures how many more patients get curative treatment after prehabilitation, so the assumed 0.5 points remains an assumption.
summary_en: B: We found no public sign of the measure in North Savo. The KYS lung cancer care pathway (2021) lists only the usual fitness tests (stair test, an exercise test with breathing measured, a 500 m walk) and says that poor general condition can rule out surgery. A FICAN East news item from 1.8.2024 says older cancer patients get a systematic geriatric assessment only in Jyväskylä and Joensuu, and that elsewhere in the region it is still being planned. A: A 2022 Cochrane review found that exercise before surgery cuts lung complications (RR 0.45), but it did not measure whether more patients become eligible for curative treatment.
unanswered_en: We found no KYS page on a prehabilitation programme or on geriatric assessment for lung cancer patients at KYS, and no study measuring how many more patients become eligible for curative treatment.
